transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I feel like no matter how hard I plan and work, I’m just not good enough to get ahead. It’s been weighing on me heavily, and I guess that's why I finally decided to come in today.
Did these feelings start after a specific work or life stress, or have you been feeling this way most days even without one? About how long has this been going on?

It really started about three years ago when I was passed over for a supervisor promotion at work, and they gave it to a younger, less-experienced coworker instead. Since then, this heavy, discouraged feeling has pretty much been my baseline almost every single day.

Do your symptoms mainly flare up when you think about that missed promotion or other specific stressors, or do they stay present most days even when nothing stressful is happening? Since they began, have they ever gone away for a couple of months at a time?

It’s definitely not just a flare-up; it feels like a constant gray cloud over me almost every day, regardless of what's happening. Since it started three years ago, this heavy feeling has been continuous and has never gone away for even a few weeks, let alone a couple of months.

During these past three years, have there been periods lasting at least two weeks when your depression became clearly worse than your usual baseline, with symptoms like losing interest, low energy, sleep or appetite changes, or trouble concentrating? Or has it stayed about the same chronic level most of the time?

It has pretty much stayed at the exact same chronic level the entire time. I haven't really noticed any specific periods where it suddenly got much worse; it's just been this continuous, heavy gray cloud as my daily norm for the last three years.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or acted more impulsively than normal? Or has your mood only been persistently low during these three years?

No, I’ve never had any periods where I felt unusually energized or happy; my mood has just been persistently low and discouraged this whole time. When I can't sleep, it's because my mind is racing with worries about work and money, and I always wake up feeling completely exhausted the next day.

Over these three years, along with feeling persistently down, have you also had at least two of these most days: low energy, low self-esteem, poor concentration or trouble making decisions, poor appetite or overeating, insomnia or sleeping too much, or feeling hopeless?

Yes, I've actually struggled with several of those most days. I feel completely hopeless about things ever changing and constantly feel like I'm just not good enough to get ahead in life. On top of that, I have a really hard time sleeping and my brain often feels like it's stuck in mud, making it tough to concentrate or make simple decisions.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistently depressed mood present nearly every day for 3 years, without remission for 2 months or more, accompanied by multiple associated symptoms of dysthymia: hopelessness, low self-esteem/inadequacy, insomnia, and poor concentration/indecisiveness. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and no superimposed major depressive episodes were identified. This pattern is most consistent with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).
